entries.topicDescription: Understanding app states, scene delegates, and background execution.

questions.questionText: What method is called when an iOS app enters the background?
questions.explanation: applicationDidEnterBackground() (UIKit) or the .background scenePhase (SwiftUI) is triggered when the app is no longer visible to the user.

questions.questionText: What's the difference between the 'inactive' and 'background' app states?
questions.explanation: Inactive means the app is still in the foreground but not receiving events (e.g. during a phone call or the app-switcher transition). Background means it's no longer visible at all.

answers.answerText: Inactive is foreground without events; background is not visible
Inactive means paused; background means terminated
They are the same state under different names
Inactive is for iPad only; background is for iPhone only

entries.topicDescription: Persistent storage and object-graph management on Apple platforms.

questions.questionText: What is an NSManagedObjectContext in Core Data?
questions.explanation: It's the in-memory scratchpad for working with managed objects — changes are tracked here before being saved to the persistent store.

answers.answerText: An in-memory scratchpad for tracking object changes before saving
The database file stored on disk

questions.questionText: What is the main advantage of SwiftData's @Model macro over Core Data's NSManagedObject subclassing?
questions.explanation: @Model turns a plain Swift class into a persisted, observable model with no separate .xcdatamodeld editor or generated subclass boilerplate — persistence is expressed directly in Swift code.

answers.answerText: Persisted models are declared directly in Swift with no separate data-model file
It removes the need for any object identity at all
It only works with SQLite, never in-memory stores
It makes every property lazy by default

entries.topicDescription: Making HTTP requests and handling APIs with URLSession and modern patterns.

questions.questionText: What class is used for making HTTP requests in iOS?
questions.explanation: URLSession is Apple's networking API for making HTTP/HTTPS requests, handling downloads, uploads, and WebSocket connections.

questions.questionText: What is App Transport Security (ATS) in iOS?
questions.explanation: ATS enforces HTTPS for all network connections by default — plain HTTP requests are blocked unless you explicitly add exceptions in Info.plist.

answers.answerText: Enforces HTTPS and blocks plain HTTP by default
Encrypts data stored on the device's disk
Prevents screenshots from being taken in the app

entries.topicDescription: Apple's declarative UI framework for building interfaces across all platforms.

questions.questionText: What is the entry point of a SwiftUI app?
questions.explanation: The @main attribute on an App struct marks it as the entry point. The 'body' property returns a Scene containing your views.

answers.answerText: A struct with @main and a body returning a Scene
The first View in the project

questions.questionText: What property wrapper makes a value observable in SwiftUI?
questions.explanation: @State creates a source of truth for value types. When the state changes, SwiftUI automatically re-renders the views that read it.

entries.topicDescription: View controllers, the responder chain, and Auto Layout in the imperative UI framework.

questions.questionText: What is the UIKit equivalent of a SwiftUI View?
questions.explanation: UIView is the base class for all visual elements in UIKit, similar to how the View protocol underlies every SwiftUI view.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of UITableViewDataSource?
questions.explanation: UITableViewDataSource supplies the data and cells for a UITableView — how many rows exist, and what each cell should display.

answers.answerText: Provides the data and cells for a UITableView
Handles tap gestures on table rows
Manages the table view's scroll position
